title: The moment we stopped understanding AI [AlexNet]
text_head:
Welch Labs traces how AlexNet's 2012 ImageNet win replaced hand-engineered vision pipelines like SIFT with learned convolutional features, then uses interpretability tools — first-layer kernel images, activation maps, feature visualization, nearest neighbors in the 4,096-dimensional penultimate layer, and Activation Atlases — to argue that the same scaled-up "dumb compute block" architecture that produced ChatGPT is precisely what made these models opaque.

AlexNet is walked through layer by layer: its first convolutional layer holds 96 kernels of size 11×11×3, small enough to render directly
